data.long_meaning: Mitesh is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Mitra', which means friend. The suffix 'esh' denotes the presence of a deity or God. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mitesh usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Mitesh was a Jain monk and a significant figure in Jainism during the 12th and 13th centuries. He wrote several important commentaries on Jain scriptures and is considered one of the greatest Jain scholars of the Middle Ages.

Mitesh is also mentioned in the 16th century Rajasthani text 'Padma Purana' as the guru of Maharaja Rao Jodha. This text relates the story of the foundation of the city of Jodhpur, where Mitesh is said to have blessed the King with his blessings and a sacred stone (known as the 'Satni Mata Stone').
